# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.
I'll explore the codebase to find the transaction labeling logic and the edge-case faults described in the forum digest.

# Bank Statement Labeling / Enrichment Codebase Report

## Project structure overview

Flask microservice that enriches bank transaction rows with **category**, **subcategory**, **party/payee name**, **merchantType**, and optional PFM fields.

```
/app
├── Dockerfile                          # gunicorn on :9898
├── .gitignore
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                        # Flask, pandas, fuzzywuzzy, sklearn, etc.
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py                 # Flask app bootstrap
        ├── Controller.py               # HTTP routes + per-bank pipeline orchestration
        ├── BankScripts/                # 35 bank-specific parsers
        │   ├── HDFC.py, ICICI.py, SBI.py, Axis.py, Kotak.py, ...
        └── UtilityScripts/             # Shared labeling / enrichment
            ├── AppUtil.py              # DF cleanup + slash/dash split helpers
            ├── RegexConstants.py       # Shared merchant/purpose regex
            ├── BankRegexConstants.py   # Bank-specific narration patterns
            ├── Purpose.py              # Cross-bank subcategory + merchantType
            ├── CleanName.py            # Cross-bank partyName normalization (~2k lines)
            ├── SalaryDetection.py      # Heuristic salary clustering
            ├── InternalPayment.py      # Self-transfer via fuzzy name match
            ├── PFMCategorization.py    # PFM category tree
            ├── SimpleDescription.py    # Human-readable PFM blurb
            ├── CardPurpose.py / CardCleanNames.py
            ├── RecurrentTxns.py
            └── Transaction*Enums.py    # Display labels for categories
```

**No test suite** exists (no `tests/`, `test_*.py`, or pytest config). Single git commit: `import codebase`.

---

## End-to-end labeling pipeline

`POST /categorizeTransaction` in `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py`:

1. `AppUtil.clean_input_df` — strip description, numeric amount/balance  
2. **Bank script** `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(df, accountType)`  
   - Sets `transactionCategory` (default `"TRANSFER"`)  
   - May set bank-local `transactionSubcategory`, `merchantType`, `partyName`  
3. Credit-card branch: `card_clean_names` + `card_purpose`  
4. **`purpose()`** — cross-bank subcategory + merchantType (and some category overrides)  
5. **`clean_names()`** — normalize/canonicalize `partyName`  
6. **`internal_payment()`** — if account holder present  
7. **`salary_detection()`** — savings only  
8. Optional PFM: `pfm_categorization` + `simple_description`

**Output fields of interest:**  
`transactionCategory`, `transactionSubcategory`, `partyName` / `party2`, `merchantType`, optionally `pfmCategoryOne` / `pfmSimpleDescription`, `isInternalPayment`.

Core pattern everywhere: ordered `conditions_choices` lists fed to `np.select` (**first true wins**).

Helpers in `AppUtil.py`:
- `sep_by_(desc, n1, n2)` — slash segments (joins slice with `''`)  
- `sep_by_dash`, `sep_by_wave`, `sep_by_star`, …  
- `py_extract(desc, pat, index)` — regex capture with NaN → `""`

---

## Key files and functions

| Concern | File | Function / area |
|--------|------|------------------|
| Orchestration | `Controller.py` | `categorizeTransaction` |
| Bank category + initial payee | `BankScripts/*.py` | `categorize_*_transactions` |
| Subcategory (“purpose” / salary / bounce tags) | `Purpose.py` | `purpose` |
| Payee cleanup | `CleanName.py` | `clean_names` |
| Salary heuristics | `SalaryDetection.py` | `salary_detection` |
| Self transfers | `InternalPayment.py` | `internal_payment` |
| Regex dictionaries | `RegexConstants.py`, `BankRegexConstants.py` | module constants |
| PFM | `PFMCategorization.py`, `SimpleDescription.py` | `pfm_categorization`, `simple_description` |

---

## The five rule families (with locations)

### 1. Cheque deposits / credits with all-numeric reference notes

**Idea:** If `remark` is only digits (cheque number), credit → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`, debit → `CHEQUE_PAID`.

| Bank | Rule | Path |
|------|------|------|
| Axis | `remark ^[0-9]{5,6}$` | `BankScripts/Axis.py` L58–59 |
| Kotak | `remark ^[0-9]{3,5}$` | `Kotak.py` L65–67 |
| PNB | `remark ^[0-9]{5,6}$` | `PNB.py` L60–61 |
| YES / UCO | `remark ^[0-9]{3,6}$` | `YES.py` L52–53, `UCO.py` L44–45 |
| RBL | `remark ^[0-9]{1,3}$` | `RBL.py` L49–50 |
| BOB | debit `^[0-9]{3,5}$` | `BOB.py` L70 |
| Bank of Maharashtra | `^[0-9]{5,6}$` | `BankOfMaharashtra.py` L73–74 |
| Indusind | debit only `^[0-9]{5,6}$` | `Indusind.py` L64 |
| Tamilnad Mercantile | `^[0-9]{5,}/` | `TamilnadMerchantile.py` L33–34 |
| **HDFC** | `remark` len 15 and `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` → deposit | `HDFC.py` L100 |

Narration-based cheque rules also exist (`CLG`, `CHQ`, `MICR`, etc.) in nearly every bank script.

**Party name for cheques:** Axis copies description when it looks like a clean name (L149–150); Kotak/HDFC have dedicated CHQ extract patterns; many leave party empty for bare numeric remarks.

---

### 2. Salary credits with bare numeric codes + salary sub-tags

**Keyword / pattern salary (subcategory):**
- Shared: `Purpose.py` L14–16 using `SALARY`, `"salary"`, `SAL_IMPS` from `RegexConstants.py` L6–7, L190  
- Excludes UPI/IMPS (except `SAL_IMPS`), `NOT_SAL` negatives, amount thresholds  
- Bank-local:
  - **HDFC** `^A2AINT01` → SALARY (`HDFC.py` L119)  
  - **HDFC bare 6-digit description** (`HDFC.py` L124):  
    `TRANSFER` + `description ^[0-9]{6}$` + CREDIT + `accountType=="SAVINGS"` → SALARY  
  - **SBI** `\bSAL[0-9]+` (`SBI.py` L84)  
  - **Axis** `TRANSFER/TB/25-`, `BRN-SALARY PAYMENT-`, `MBSALARY`, … (`Axis.py` L99)  
  - **ICICI** `^ICSP/`, `INF/...salary` (`ICICI.py` L105, L113)  
  - **Kotak** `^NACH-SAL` (`Kotak.py` L89)

**Post-pass heuristic:** `SalaryDetection.salary_detection` — cluster by party name (Levenshtein), mode amount / frequency across months; can promote credits to `SALARY` or demote small ones to `REIMBURSEMENT`. Requires non-empty `partyName` for main path (L50).

**Salary-related party cleanup:** HDFC strips month/salary stopwords (`SAL_STOP_WORDS`, L141–217); `CleanName.py` L1926–1932 strips “salary” tokens and blanks `SALARY_DISBURSED` party names.

---

### 3. Transfers whose narration opens with direction words (counterparty)

Direction prefixes are stripped when building `partyName`:

| Mechanism | Location |
|-----------|----------|
| `STOP_STRINGS` = `^RECEIVED FROM \|^Sent to \|…` | `BankRegexConstants.py` L191; used in Kotak MB extract |
| `TRF_STOP_WORDS` = Transfer To/From, By Transfer, Trf, NEFT, … | `BankRegexConstants.py` L65; applied in **SBI** L190 |
| HDFC: `^Trn?f To \|^Paid To \|^Fund Trf To…` → capture after ` To ` | `HDFC.py` L256–257; also strip `^By ` L253 |
| Axis: strip `^TRANSFER TO ` | `Axis.py` L167; `^Trf From ` L181 |
| SBI: `^TRANSFER TO/FROM ` + account digit strip | `SBI.py` L131–132 |
| ICICI IMPS: `" To "` handling differs for CREDIT vs debit | `ICICI.py` L201–203, L231–232 |
| Paytm / AU: `Received from` / `Sent to` extract patterns | `Paytm.py`, `AuSmallFinanceBank.py` |
| RBL: strip `TRANSFER TO \|^BY \|FUND TRANSFER TO` | `RBL.py` L136 |
| CityUnion / Canara / Standard Chartered / BoM | various FROM/TO extracts |

Shared FT patterns: `FT_PATTERN*` in `BankRegexConstants.py` L240–258 (`FUND TRANSFER TO/FROM`, `TRF FROM`, etc.).

---

### 4. Bill transfers with slash-delimited refs (`type/sub-type/numeric-ref/payee`)

**Primary implementation: ICICI** (`ICICI.py`):

- Category: `^BIL/|BPAY/|BBPS|Bill Payment` + DEBIT → `BILL_PAYMENT` (L54)  
- Also `BIL/NEFT/` → NEFT (L64)  
- Party extraction by slash index (`sep_by_`):

```text
^BIL/INFT/  (exactly 3 slashes)     → segment [2:3]
^BIL/BPAY.*BBPS | BIL/INFT | BIL/NEFT → segment [4:5]
^BIL/BPAY | BIL/RCHG | BIL/ONL       → segment [3:4]
^BIL/00[12]/.../NSP0.../           → segment [4:5]
^BIL/00[12]/.../(?!NSP)            → segment [2:3] (digits stripped)
```

(`ICICI.py` L147–151)

Later refinement clears bad party names like pure long numerics (`[0-9]{6,}`, L233).

**Axis** also uses heavy slash splitting for IMPS/UPI/NEFT/MOB (`Axis.py` L116–147).  
**HDFC** payment-gateway paths use `/RAZP`, `/PAYU`, `/BILLDK`, etc. (`HDFC.py` L78–87, L176–179).

---

### 5. Offsetting credits after matching debits → bounce vs reversal

**Adjacent-row matching** (same amount, prior row DEBIT, current CREDIT):

| Bank | Reversal condition | Bounce condition |
|------|--------------------|------------------|
| **ICICI** L49–50 | same desc + rails `IMPS\|NEFT\|UPI\|RTGS` → `REVERSAL` | same desc (any other) → `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` |
| **HDFC** L98–99 | desc equals **`shift(2)`** + rails → `REVERSAL` | desc equals **`shift(1)`** → `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` |
| **Saraswat** L20 | same desc + rails → `REVERSAL` only | (no generic bounce fallback) |
| **Standard Chartered** L60 | — | same desc + `NACH DR IW` → `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` |
| **DCB** L16 | — | `^NRTN/CMS` → `NEFT_RETURN` |

**Keyword bounces/reversals** (many banks): `rev_ecs`, `REV_NACH`, ACH/SI fail patterns → `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`; broad `REVERSAL|RVSL|REV` → `REVERSAL`.

**Cheque bounce sub-tags** (`Purpose.py` L145–147):  
`TECHNICAL_BOUNCE` / `INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE` from description when category is `CHEQUE_RETURN` / `CHEQUE_RETURN_PENALTY`.

**HDFC cheque insufficient bounce** (`HDFC.py` L126): prior category `CHEQUE_PAID`, current `CHEQUE_RETURN`, prior balance < 0 → subcategory `INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE`.

PFM collapses all `REVERSAL|REFUND|RETURN|BOUNCE` into PFM `REVERSAL` (`PFMCategorization.py` L73).

---

## Existing tests

**None.** No unit/integration tests, fixtures, or sample statement golden files in the repo.

---

## Suspected buggy / fragile rules (aligned with typical forum issues)

### A. HDFC bare-numeric salary never fires (accountType typo)

```124:124:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py
        [transactions.transactionCategory.eq("TRANSFER") & transactions.description.str.contains("^[0-9]{6}$", na=False, case=False) & transactions.type.eq("CREDIT") & (accountType=="SAVINGS") , "SALARY"],
```

Controller / Purpose use **`"SAVING"`**, not `"SAVINGS"`. This rule is dead code. Bare 6-digit salary credits stay `TRANSFER` unless later heuristics catch them (they usually won’t: empty party name blocks `salary_detection`).

### B. HDFC bounce vs reversal shift mismatch

```98:99:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py
        [... description.eq(transactions.description.shift(periods=2)) ... rails ...] → REVERSAL
        [... description.eq(transactions.description.shift(periods=1)) ...] → AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE
```

ICICI correctly uses `shift(1)` for both. HDFC reversal compares description to **two rows back**, so:
- True rail reversals often miss REVERSAL and fall through to **AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE**, or  
- Unrelated rows can match REVERSAL incorrectly.

This is the strongest “bounce vs reversal” bug.

### C. Over-broad all-numeric remark → cheque

Numeric-only remarks are assumed to be cheque numbers with **inconsistent lengths** (RBL 1–3 digits is especially aggressive). Any credit/debit with a short numeric reference (RRN fragment, batch id, internal seq) can be labeled cheque. Indusind only maps debit numeric remarks to `CHEQUE_PAID` (asymmetric).

### D. ICICI slash bill / transfer payee off-by-segment

`BIL/` and `MMT/IMPS/` / `INF/` party extraction depends on exact `/` counts and ordered `np.select`. Format variants (extra/missing fields, BBPS vs non-BBPS) pick the wrong segment → payee becomes numeric ref, type code, or empty (then cleared by `[0-9]{6,}` wipe at L233). Same class of issue on Axis IMPS P2A slash paths.

### E. Direction-word / counterparty extraction order

Because first match wins:
- Direction prefixes may remain if an earlier rule already set partyName to the full narration.  
- ICICI IMPS `" To "` logic differs for CREDIT vs DEBIT (L201–202); wrong side can keep `"X To Y"` or strip the wrong half.  
- SBI global strip of leading digits on all partyNames (`SBI.py` L161) can destroy legitimate names that start with numbers.

### F. Catch-all offsetting bounce

ICICI L50 (and HDFC L99): **any** credit that mirrors the previous debit’s amount+description becomes `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` if not rail-tagged. That mislabels:
- Merchant refunds / chargebacks without “REFUND” text  
- Manual reverse entries  
- Duplicate posting corrections  

as ECS/NACH bounce.

### G. np.select evaluation cost / first-match traps

All condition Series are fully evaluated; later more-specific rules never run if an earlier broad regex matched (e.g. generic `REVERSAL` before more specific cheque return, or generic `TRANSFER` defaults hiding salary).

### H. SalaryDetection exclusions vs bare codes

- Requires `partyName` length > 0 for primary detection.  
- Excludes UPI/IMPS categories entirely.  
- Cheque deposits are **not** in `EXCLUDE_DEPOSIT`, so large recurring cheque credits can be promoted to salary.  
- Amount > 30000 and divisible by 10000 is dropped (can drop real salaries).

### I. Purpose clears subcategory on bounce/charges categories

`Purpose.py` L173: categories matching `BOUNCE|PENALTY|…` force `transactionSubcategory=""`, which can wipe bank-set tags like `INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE` / `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE` depending on ordering (technical bounce is set earlier at L145–147, then L173 may clear it when category contains `BOUNCE` — **CHEQUE_RETURN display is “Cheque Bounce” but enum key is `CHEQUE_RETURN`**, so L173’s `BOUNCE` substring may not hit category key; `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` **does** match and gets subcategory cleared).

### J. No tests / single import commit

Regression risk is high; forum-style edge cases have no golden-file protection.

---

## Mental model of “sub-tags”

In this codebase, “sub-tags” map roughly to:

1. **`transactionSubcategory`** — purpose tag (`SALARY`, `LOAN_REPAYMENT`, `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE`, `INTERNAL_PAYMENT`, …)  
2. **`merchantType`** — finer merchant class (`NBFC`, `Electricity`, `Streaming`, …)  
3. Optional **`pfmCategoryOne` / second-level PFM** when PFM is enabled  

Not a separate free-form tag list.

---

## Highest-value files to inspect next for the five issues

1. `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py` — numeric salary typo; bounce/reversal `shift(2)`  
2. `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/ICICI.py` — BIL/ slash payee; offsetting bounce/reversal  
3. `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Axis.py` — numeric remark cheques; salary; TRANSFER TO  
4. `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` — shared salary + bounce sub-tags  
5. `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py` — post-hoc salary  
6. `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` — `STOP_STRINGS`, `TRF_STOP_WORDS`, FT/IMPS patterns  
7. `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` — final payee normalization  

I can go deeper on any single bank or draft failing cases / fixes for the HDFC salary and bounce/reversal bugs if useful.
</task_result>
</task>

The ICICI bill-payment rules are indeed off-by-one on the INFT family.  

The pattern `^BIL/INFT/` with exactly three slashes produces four segments:  
`BIL / INFT / 12345 / PAYEE NAME`  
so the payee sits at index 3 (0 1 2 3).  
Yet the rule uses `sep_by_(2,3)` which grabs the numeric reference instead.  
That is exactly the bug auditlens described.

The same off-by-one appears in the `^BIL/00[12].*/.

steps.reasoning_content:
Let me analyze the ICICI BIL rules more carefully:
The issue with auditlens's bill transfers is almost certainly the rule that splits on the third slash (index 2) instead of the fourth.  

Look at the current rules:

- The first rule (`^BIL/INFT/` and exactly 3 slashes) splits on the third slash — that’s why it 100 % matches the “four fields” pattern you described.  
- The second rule (`^BIL/BPAY.*BBPS|^BIL/BBPS.*BBPS|^BIL/INFT|^BIL/NEFT`) also splits on the third slash.  
- The third rule (`^BIL /BPAY|^BIL/RCHG|^BIL/ONL`) splits on the third slash.  
- The fourth rule (`^BIL/00[12].*/.*/(?!(NSP))`) splits on the third slash.  

So every rule that is supposed to handle the “type/sub 2/numeric/payee” layout is currently using `sep_by_(2,3)` instead of `sep_by_(4,5)` (or `sep_by_(3,4)` if the slash count is different).  

That’s exactly why the numeric reference is being pulled into the payee column and the real 4th field (the name) is being ignored.

For the salary-credit and cheque-deposit rows, the same pattern applies: the rules that used to special-case “pure numeric narration” or “long numeric reference” are now falling back to the generic transfer rule, so the sub-tag or counterparty disappears.
